newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Bankgesellschaft eyes takeovers, profits up.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Bankgesellschaft eyes takeovers, profits up.

text.p: Germany's Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG on Friday reiterated its interest in taking over another bank as it reported a significant improvement in operating profit in the first four months of the year.

But management board chairman Wolfgang Rupf told shareholders that the bank, which is thought to be interested in taking over the Frankfurt-based BHF Bank, had not started concrete merger negotiations.

Bankgesellschaft's operating profit before risk provisions rose around 34 percent to 586 million marks ($337.8 million) in the four months to April, Rupf said, although that could not be extrapolated for the year as it included returns from securities.
He said the bank had estimated risk provisions for the year at 500 million marks, compared with 2.5 billion marks in 1996.
Bankgesellschaft's merger talks are at present focused on Norddeutsche Landesbank, the regional state-owned bank with which it is considering a fusion.
However Rupf also repeated that the bank was keen to find a partner in investment banking.
Comments like these have sparked widespread speculation that Bankgesellschaft might buy BHF.

However the head of BHF-Bank on Thursday dismissed speculation that the bank might be taken over by Bankgesellschaft, arguing that it did not make sense for it to becaome part of a state-owned banking group.
Bankgesellschaft is 56.8 percent owned by the city of Berlin.
"Nobody has spoken to us about it (a takeover)," BHF management board chairman Ernst Michel Kruse told reporters in Berlin.
Bankgesellschaft itself has said all along that it was not presently in takeover talks.
